review_type: focused remote source and test review
scope: Actual reduced-motion handling and non-color-only selection/status cues in StudioView, StudioGuideView and StudioPlanMarkers, compared with StudioAppAccessibilityUITests.

checks.name: startup and acceptance review
checks.details: Read AGENTS.md and all named startup documents plus docs/acceptance/m02-m03-code.md remotely at the pinned commit. This task has no host execution; scripts and runtime checks were not run.

checks.name: reduced-motion implementation trace
checks.details: The Scene toolbar Meter button sets showMeter=true and increments meterNavigationRequest. Its onChange scrolls to the identified meterPanel. With accessibilityReduceMotion true it calls proxy.scrollTo directly; otherwise it wraps the same scroll in withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration:0.25)). The inspected StudioView contains this single explicit animation block. StudioGuideView and StudioPlanMarkers contain no explicit animation calls.

checks.name: selection cues
checks.details: View/study choices show a checkmark and expose isSelected. Light-list selection uses checkmark.circle.fill versus circle plus isSelected. Plan exposes a literal Selected: <name> caption; markers add isSelected and a 2-point versus 1-point border, and selected markers render above unselected markers. The Plan therefore does not depend on color alone.

checks.name: status and guide semantics
checks.details: Project status says Saved data protected, Saved locally or Unsaved changes; pending operations include a textual progressTitle beside ProgressView. Meter disclosure exposes Expanded/Collapsed plus a matching hint. Guide uses text titles/summaries, labeled navigation links and a Done action; it has no custom selected/status state requiring an additional non-color cue.

checks.name: test-source comparison
checks.details: The required workflow runs default and largest accessibility text sizes; checks Unsaved changes text; verifies initial mode selected traits; taps Fill on Plan and checks its literal selected caption, then checks Fill/Key list traits and checkmark.circle.fill containment. It taps openMeter and verifies meter content. It does not set or toggle Reduce Motion, assert scroll animation behavior, directly inspect the selected Plan-marker trait/border, or exercise the guide. No runtime result is inferred from these assertions.

conclusion: No concrete product defect established in this focused source review. Actual Reduce Motion handling is present for the custom Meter navigation scroll, and inspected selection/status paths include non-color cues. Missing direct reduced-motion test coverage is recorded as an evidence limit, not a demonstrated behavior defect or a reason for code churn.
limitations: Host unavailable; no scripts, builds, tests, simulator/device interactions or screenshot review executed.
The reduced-motion source branch applies to the custom Meter navigation scroll; this is not proof about system-provided navigation/sheet transitions or animation behavior in other files.
Test review is scoped to UITests/StudioAppAccessibilityUITests.swift; it is not a repository-wide proof of absence of other test coverage.
This report completes a source review only and does not independently establish M03 acceptance, a completed platform accessibility audit or real-device behavior.
mutations: Only this unreferenced JSON report blob is created; no source, tree, branch, ref, test or acceptance changes.
